papers.title: Environmental and biotic drivers of Aedes albopictus spatiotemporal distribution in a subtropical city: A major transit hub on Argentina’s triple border
papers.summary: Biophysical and ecological factors are known to shape the distribution of mosquito vectors, yet their interaction across heterogeneous and rapidly transforming landscapes remains insufficiently understood.  We assessed the occurrence of Aedes albopictus in relation to environmental and biotic drivers in the Iguazú Department, Misiones Province, Argentina, within the tri-border region shared with Brazil and Paraguay, a key epidemiological corridor for arboviral transmission.
papers.mainFinding: These findings provide a robust basis for targeted surveillance and highlight the need for coordinated, cross-border vector management strategies in rapidly transforming subtropical regions.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Infrared thermal imaging to determine temperature parameters of dengue vector habitats across ecological regions of Nepal: a pilot feasibility study
papers.summary: Dengue is a major vector-borne disease in Nepal, driven by container-breeding Aedes mosquitoes that thrive in domestic, urban settings.  Its risk is increasing from the lowland Terai to the Hill and Mountain regions due to urbanisation and global warming.
papers.mainFinding: Thermal imaging shows promise for the field characterisation of mosquito breeding sites, but it is not interchangeable with standard thermometry without qualification, including calibration and uncertainty analysis.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Plant-based Mosquito Repellents against Adult Mosquitoes
papers.summary: Mosquito-borne diseases remain a major public health concern, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions, creating a continued need for effective and sustainable vector-control approaches.  Plant-based repellents offer a potentially affordable and environmentally compatible alternative to conventional synthetic mosquito-control products.
papers.mainFinding: Further work should standardise formulation ratios, characterise active compounds, assess smoke safety, establish adequate replication, and evaluate performance under field conditions.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Temperature variation as a driver of Wolbachia release efficacy: implications for dengue control in warming climates
papers.summary: Background Wolbachia-based control methods reduce dengue transmission by suppressing Aedes aegypti populations or blocking viral replication, yet their effectiveness across the climatic conditions of endemic regions remains poorly understood.  Seasonal and interannual temperature changes shape mosquito dynamics, but how Wolbachia releases perform during anomalous events such as El Nino or heatwaves is largely unknown a gap that limits our ability to optimize release strategies and predict intervention success across different climates.
papers.mainFinding: By elucidating the mechanistic interplay among temperature, Wolbachia, and dengue, our findings help refine Wolbachia release programs to suit different climatic conditions, thereby strengthening dengue control as climate variability intensifies.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Immature anophelines and their habitat characteristics in an urban setting of central Ethiopia
papers.summary: Effective immature malaria vector control requires a comprehensive understanding of the relationship between Anopheles larvae and their habitats.  In this study, we assessed habitat characteristics of Anopheles larvae and species composition of adult anophelines emerged from pupae.
papers.mainFinding: The occurrence of multiple Anopheles species and the presence of favorable habitats indicate the need for implementing larval surveillance and targeted larval source management practices as part of integrated malaria vector control strategies.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Early-evening indoor and outdoor foraging by major malaria vectors in Nchelenge, Zambia
papers.summary: Despite a decade of indoor residual spraying, malaria remains holoendemic in Nchelenge District in northern Zambia.  This study examined the hypothesis that the intransigence of malaria in Nchelenge District is due in part to early evening and outdoor foraging of local anopheline species.
papers.mainFinding: Overall, this study adds to the growing body of evidence that malaria transmission is not limited to late-night, indoor settings in Nchelenge District, Zambia.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Functional Deorphanization and Subtype-Selective Pharmacology of Three Tyramine Receptors in the Disease Vector, Aedes aegypti
papers.summary: Biogenic amines such as tyramine (TA) and octopamine (OA) are central regulators of insect physiology and behaviour, acting through G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) to control reproduction, locomotion, metabolism, olfaction and hydromineral homeostasis.  Although TA was once considered solely a biosynthetic precursor to OA, it is now recognized as an independent signaling molecule acting through distinct tyramine receptors (TARs).
papers.mainFinding: These findings establish that AaTAR1, AaTAR2 and AaTAR3 are bona fide functional tyramine receptors, define their ligand selectivity and subtype-specific pharmacology, and provide a comparative framework for understanding mosquito tyraminergic signaling, highlighting their potential as targets for next-generation vector control strategies.

papers.title: Distinct Swimming Behaviours in Pupae of Aedes, Anopheles and Culex Mosquitoes
papers.summary: The study quantified surface-swimming behaviour in pupae from 11 mosquito species. Aedes pupae generally moved slowly but frequently and explored more, whereas Anopheles and especially Culex pupae moved less often but swam faster and farther during each movement bout.
papers.mainFinding: Mosquito pupae are not an ecologically passive stage; their movement strategies differ consistently among genera and may reflect adaptation to different aquatic habitats.
papers.whyItMatters: Pupal mobility can change exposure to predators, sampling devices, habitat edges, and emergence conditions. It is a strong conceptual and methodological paper for interpreting predator encounters and control efficiency in urban-rural mesocosms.
papers.readFirstReason: Directly connects Culex aquatic behaviour with predator encounters and the interpretation of mesocosm control experiments.

papers.title: Development of a Novel Immune Gene Array to Assess Mosquito Gene Expression During Arbovirus Infection
papers.summary: Assessing mosquito vector competence for emerging arboviruses, including the underlying determinants of infection, is a foundational line of investigation towards understanding arbovirus transmission dynamics and vector–virus interactions.  We developed a novel quantitative immune gene array that measures the relative expression of 22 immune genes with functional representation across five major immune pathways using quantitative reverse-transcriptase polymerase chain reaction.
papers.mainFinding: This new tool will be broadly applicable for assessing mosquito immune profiles for arbovirus infection across major immune genes in five key pathways, as well as generating comparable results across mosquito and arbovirus systems.
papers.whyItMatters: Conceptual or methodological relevance to mosquito eco-evolution and vector ecology.

papers.title: Herramienta automatizada de segmentación y clasificación del paisaje urbano para la vigilancia eco-epidemiológica con drones
papers.summary: Este estudio propone una herramienta automatizada para la segmentación y clasificación del paisaje urbano asociado a criaderos de Aedes aegypti, utilizando imágenes aéreas RGB tomadas por dron en Tapachula, Chiapas, México.  Bajo un enfoque de Análisis de Imágenes Basado en Objetos (OBIA), las imágenes fueron segmentadas en superpixeles mediante el algoritmo SLIC, y se extrajeron características estadísticas, de borde y de textura para cada objeto.
papers.mainFinding: De los clasificadores evaluados (KNN, SVM y MLP), la red neuronal MLP obtuvo el mejor desempeño global (F1-score ponderado) y el menor tiempo de predicción.
papers.whyItMatters: Relevant to separating genetic, plastic and environmental components of urban-rural trait differences.

papers.title: Oviposition Activity and Ecological Patterns of Medically Important Culicidae in an Agroforestry System in the Atlantic Forest, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
papers.summary: A 47-month field study used elevated ovitraps to examine mosquito oviposition around an agroforestry–forest interface in Rio de Janeiro. Oviposition varied strongly by season and species, with sylvatic mosquitoes occurring in modified habitat and Aedes albopictus entering forest habitat.
papers.mainFinding: Mosquito oviposition and habitat use at the agroforestry–forest interface were strongly species- and season-dependent.
papers.whyItMatters: The sampling design is useful for ovitrap placement, habitat surveillance, and oviposition-site management, while its observational nature means it does not isolate causal oviposition cues or demonstrate adaptation.

papers.title: Establishment of a Stable Anopheles melas Laboratory Colony for the First Time and Characterization of Its Pyrethroid Resistance Profile in Senegal
papers.summary: A colony founded from 26 PCR-confirmed Anopheles melas females was stabilized through generation F17 by optimizing water salinity and communal oviposition. WHO tube bioassays found pyrethroid resistance that declined markedly after piperonyl butoxide exposure, implicating P450-mediated metabolism.
papers.mainFinding: A difficult brackish-water vector was maintained over many generations while retaining measurable and mechanistically informative resistance phenotypes.
papers.whyItMatters: The salinity and communal-oviposition protocol may inform difficult mosquito colonization and multigenerational assays, although the species and coastal ecology differ substantially from Culex pipiens.

papers.summary: Abstract Background Culex pipiens pallens is a significant vector of mosquito-borne diseases, and its autogenous trait exerts a critical impact on population expansion and disease transmission risks.  Understanding the regulatory effect of gut-specific symbiotic bacteria on the autogeny of Cx.
papers.mainFinding: These findings not only provide an important microbial regulatory perspective for understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying autogeny in mosquitoes, but also offer potential targets for the development of novel symbiont-based biocontrol strategies against mosquito-borne diseases.

papers.title: Importance of Rabbit’s Blood Meal in the Assessment of Factors which Influence Vector Susceptibility to Insecticides
papers.summary: The understanding of the factors that influence vector susceptibility to insecticides is important.  The current study aimed at investigating the importance of rabbit’s blood meal in the assessment of factors that influence vector susceptibility to Lambda-Cyhalothrin (Karate, as a commercial product name).

papers.title: Insight into eco-epidemiological traits of European native vector mosquitoes for disease transmission
papers.taxon: Culex pipiens and other native European mosquitoes
papers.summary: This open-access primer synthesizes the distribution, larval habitats, host-seeking and host preferences, overwintering strategies, hybridization, and vector competence of native European mosquitoes. It places native Culex mosquitoes at the centre of Europe’s expanding West Nile virus risk and identifies major ecological and surveillance gaps.
papers.mainFinding: European transmission risk is increasingly shaped by native mosquito vectors, while incomplete information on their ecological ranges and life-history traits still limits surveillance and risk assessment.
papers.whyItMatters: This is the strongest framing paper for connecting Belgian Culex pipiens ecology, urban habitat use, host interactions, climate sensitivity, and population structure to WNV emergence and spatial expansion in Europe.
papers.readFirstReason: The most direct synthesis of native European mosquito ecology, Culex involvement, and changing WNV transmission risk.
papers.vectorSpecies: Native European mosquitoes, especially Culex spp. including Culex pipiens
papers.hostSpecies: Avian reservoir hosts; humans and horses as incidental hosts
papers.studyPeriod: Primer and evidence synthesis; WNV distribution examples include data through 3 December 2025
papers.europeanTransmissionRisk: Shows how well-adapted native Culex vectors support sustained WNV transmission and expansion into newly affected European regions.

papers.title: Evolution under the city’s shadow: reproductive divergence of urban and rural great tits revealed by a common garden experiment
papers.summary: Urban- and forest-origin great tits were collected as unincubated eggs, raised under standardized conditions, and bred in a common environment. Urban–forest differences in laying date disappeared, egg-size differences persisted, and clutch-size patterns reversed relative to wild populations.
papers.mainFinding: Urban reproductive divergence combined plastic responses, persistent inherited or early-life effects, and counter-gradient variation that was masked in the field.
papers.whyItMatters: It is an unusually close methodological analogue for separating genetic, plastic, maternal, and environmental contributions in Belgian urban-rural Culex pipiens common-garden experiments.

papers.title: Mosquito Control: Importance of Biological Alternatives in Integrated Vector Management Approaches
papers.summary: Mosquito-borne diseases continue to pose major global public health challenges, necessitating the development of sustainable, environmentally safe, and effective vector control strategies.  Conventional reliance on chemical insecticides has led to increasing concerns regarding insecticide resistance, environmental contamination, and adverse effects on non-target organisms.
papers.mainFinding: Integrating these biological methods with existing vector control strategies provides a sustainable and ecologically sound approach to reducing mosquito-borne disease transmission.

papers.title: Vector competence across Aedes aegypti populations shaped by host-preference adaptation and host-pathogen interactions
papers.summary: ABSTRACT Aedes aegypti is the principal vector for yellow fever, dengue, Zika, and chikungunya viruses.  Although this mosquito continues to expand its global range, its intrinsic ability to acquire, support the replication of, and transmit specific viruses—known as vector competence (VC)—varies across populations.
papers.mainFinding: Finally, we evaluate emerging insights into the molecular mechanisms that may drive this variation, with emphasis on the mosquito virome and the antiviral RNA interference pathways, and how these, in turn, help shape the genetic architecture associated with the intrinsic capacity to transmit arboviruses.
papers.whyItMatters: Relevant to separating genetic, plastic and environmental components of urban-rural trait differences.

papers.title: Iron Homeostasis and Reproduction: Unveiling the Microbiome–Gut–Brain Axis Connection in the Mosquito Anopheles culicifacies
papers.summary: Our study investigated how adult female Anopheles culicifacies mosquitoes regulate systemic iron homeostasis after blood feeding, a process essential for reproduction, and revealed striking parallels to iron deficiency disorders in mammals.  This study identifies that coordinated transcriptional regulation of ferritin and transferrin plays a crucial role in follicle development and egg maturation.
papers.mainFinding: In summary, our research provides the first molecular proof and a new conceptual understanding of how iron metabolism disorders may affect microbiome–gut–brain-axis communication and, in turn, reproductive outcomes.

papers.title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis: From Molecular Profiling to Ecotope-Specific Larvicidal Efficacy Against Laboratory Aedes aegypti and Wild Mosquito Populations
papers.taxon: Aedes aegypti and wild mosquito populations
papers.summary: Three native Bacillus thuringiensis subsp. israelensis H14 strains were molecularly profiled and tested against laboratory Aedes aegypti and wild mosquito larvae. Controlled exposure produced approximately 95–96% mortality within 48 hours, followed by comparisons across forest and steppe mosquito populations.
papers.mainFinding: The Bti strains combined stable Cry and Cyt toxin production with strong larvicidal activity, although efficacy varied with strain and ecological setting.
papers.whyItMatters: The study offers endpoints and assay structure for testing context-dependent mosquito control, but laboratory and regional field efficacy should not be treated as proof of persistence or non-target safety in Belgian urban ponds.
